name: Pyramids of Giza
category: Ancient Monument / Necropolis / UNESCO World Heritage Site
historical_description: The Pyramids of Giza form the last surviving wonder of the ancient Seven Wonders of the World. The plateau holds three main pyramids — the Great Pyramid of Khufu, the Pyramid of Khafre, and the smaller Pyramid of Menkaure — along with several subsidiary queens' pyramids, mastaba tombs of nobles, the causeway and valley temples, and the Great Sphinx. Built as royal tombs during Egypt's Old Kingdom, the complex represents the peak of pyramid-building technology and remains the most iconic image of ancient Egyptian civilization. The site has fascinated travelers, scholars, and conquerors for over 4,500 years, from Herodotus to Napoleon.

construction_details.duration_estimate: The Great Pyramid is estimated to have taken around 20 years to build
construction_details.materials: Limestone blocks (local quarried and fine Tura limestone casing), granite (from Aswan) for internal chambers

great_pyramid_dimensions.estimated_blocks: approximately 2.3 million stone blocks, averaging 2.5 tonnes each

construction_details.architects: Traditionally associated with the vizier Hemiunu for the Great Pyramid
construction_details.construction_theories: Ramps (straight, spiral, or internal), levers, and large organized labor forces of paid workers (not slaves, per archaeological evidence from workers' villages) are the leading theories

opening_hours.interior_pyramid_access: Limited daily visitor quota for entering the Great Pyramid's interior chambers; last entry typically 1 hour before closing
opening_hours.notes: Hours can shift slightly for religious holidays (Ramadan, Eid) and are set by the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

ticket_price.notes: Prices are set by Egypt's Supreme Council of Antiquities and are revised periodically (last major revision effective January 2025). Interior access to Khafre's and Menkaure's pyramids is ticketed separately and subject to availability. Always confirm current prices via the official egymonuments.com portal or at the gate before visiting.

best_visiting_time.time_of_day: Early morning (opening time) or 1-2 hours before closing, to avoid heat and tour bus crowds
best_visiting_time.season: October to April (cooler, more comfortable daytime temperatures)
best_visiting_time.avoid: Midday in June–August, when temperatures often exceed 38°C (100°F)

interesting_facts: The Great Pyramid of Khufu was the tallest man-made structure in the world for roughly 3,800 years, until the completion of Lincoln Cathedral's spire in the 14th century CE.

The pyramids were originally covered in polished white Tura limestone casing that would have made them gleam in the sun; most of this casing was stripped in later centuries for building material in Cairo.
The Great Sphinx is carved from a single block of limestone bedrock and is thought to depict Pharaoh Khafre with a lion's body.
Despite popular myth, archaeological evidence from nearby workers' villages shows the pyramids were built by paid laborers, not slaves.
The three main pyramids are aligned with remarkable precision to the cardinal points (north, south, east, west).
A newly-built Grand Egyptian Museum sits just 2 km from the plateau and offers panoramic views of the pyramids from its galleries.
unesco_status: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Memphis and its Necropolis – the Pyramid Fields from Giza to Dahshur' (inscribed 1979)
accessibility_notes: Uneven sandy and rocky terrain; wheelchair access is limited on the plateau itself, though a paved viewing area is available. Pyramid interiors involve steep, low-ceilinged passages and are not wheelchair accessible.
nearest_airport: Cairo International Airport (CAI), approx. 30–40 km away
